# Tobit Chapter 9 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

## Overview
Chapter 9 is the shortest chapter in Tobit (6 verses). Despite its brevity, the three agents diverged on 7 translation decisions, primarily regarding: the financial term cheirographon, the register of Tobit's anticipated grief (v. 3), the treatment of sealed bags (v. 4), Tobias's action upon arrival (v. 5), and the structure of Gabael's blessing (v. 6).

---

## Disagreement Table

| Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA Resolution |
|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|-------------------|
| 9:2 | Toponym form | "Rages-of Media" | "Rages in Media" | "Rages in Media" | "Rages in Media" — LOGOS/PNEUMA agreement; natural English preposition |
| 9:3 | Degree of Tobit's grief | "he will be greatly grieved" | "he will be deeply grieved" | "it will break his heart" | "he will be deeply grieved" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's idiom is too colloquial for the chapter's register |
| 9:4 | cheirographon | preserved as "the cheirograph" with note | "the bond" | "the promissory note" | "the bond" — LOGOS; translates rather than transliterates (EMET), avoids anachronism (PNEUMA) |
| 9:4 | Sealed bags | "bags-sealed-with-their-seals" (literal doubling) | "bags with their seals intact" | "moneybags still sealed, just as they had been left" | "bags with their seals intact" — LOGOS; captures the legal significance without PNEUMA's narrative padding |
| 9:5 | Tobias's action | "Tobias blessed his wife" | "Tobias blessed his wife" | "Tobias went to embrace his wife" | "Tobias blessed his wife" — EMET/LOGOS; PNEUMA substitutes an action not in the Greek |
| 9:6 | Covenantal repetition | "children-of your-children, and the-children-of your-children" | "your children's children, and your children's children's children" | "their children, and their children's children — blessing upon blessing" | Full repetition preserved (LOGOS); PNEUMA's "blessing upon blessing" is a paraphrase |
| 9:6 | ep' aletheias in final clause | "love you in truth" | "love you in truth" | "truly loves you" | "love you in truth" — maintains verbal parallel with 8:7 where the same phrase appears |

---

## Notes

### The cheirographon (v. 4)
This is one of the most commercially specific terms in the Deuterocanon. The cheirographon was a handwritten receipt or promissory note — the ancient equivalent of a signed contract. Tobit gave this to Gabael when he deposited the money (Tob 1:14), and Raphael now uses it to redeem the funds. EMET's decision to preserve the Greek term is defensible but creates an opacity in the reading. LOGOS's "bond" is the clearest English legal equivalent that does not project a specifically modern institution. PNEUMA's "promissory note" is also accurate but slightly anachronistic in connotation.

### Verse 5: "Blessed his wife"
PNEUMA's substitution of "went to embrace" for "blessed" is a significant departure. The Greek verb eulogesen means "to bless/speak well of" — it is a formal act, not simply a physical greeting. In the narrative, Tobias's blessing of Sarah echoes the blessings throughout the chapter and knits the scene together thematically.

*— SOPHIA*
